# FM301 conformance goldens

Golden summaries of what xradar 0.12.0 and arm_pyart 2.2.5 return for real radar files, for the
FM301 conformance tests of plan F.4 (wave 2, stream F) and
spec 4.3. The Rust side builds the FM301 view of the same file (`docs/design/fm301-model.md`
section 12) and compares names, dimensions, attributes and values against these files.

Generated by `tools/fm301_golden.py`. The schema is documented in that script's docstring.

```bash
PY=<venv with xradar 0.12.0, arm_pyart 2.2.5, metpy 1.7.1>/python
$PY tools/fm301_golden.py --verify          # regenerate everything, cross-checking the readers
$PY tools/fm301_golden.py --check --offline # fail if a golden is stale
$PY tools/fm301_golden.py <id> ...          # regenerate some cases
```

Files are resolved through the testdata manifests (committed copy, else the
`recast-radar-testdata` download cache) and verified by SHA-256.

## Layout

| Path | Content |
|---|---|
| `xradar/<id>.json` | `open_*_datatree` output: views `time` (`first_dim="time"`, `mask_and_scale=False`) and `auto` (`first_dim="auto"`, `mask_and_scale=False`), plus the default decoded open, all with `optional_groups=True` |
| `pyart/<id>.json` | `read_nexrad_archive(linear_interp=False)`, `aux_io.read_odim_h5` or `read_cfradial` output: Radar metadata, coordinate and instrument variables, per-sweep field statistics and hashes |
| `index.json` | cases, categories, reader options, software versions, statuses |

The `time` view is the encoded form that design note 12.3 says F.4 compares
(`FirstDim::Time`, `decode = false`); the `auto` view pins xradar's default ray order and
dimension names (`FirstDim::Auto`). Every hash is SHA-256 over little-endian elements in row-major
order with NaN canonicalized, so a Rust array with the same dtype, shape, ray order and values
hashes identically.

## Cases

| id | reader | categories | xradar | Py-ART |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `l2-ktlx-20240315-000217` | nexrad | modern dual-pol, SAILS x3 (Build 22.0, VCP 212) | ok | ok |
| `l2-kdvn-20200810-180401` | nexrad | modern dual-pol, MESO-SAILS x2 (Build 18.2, 8-bit ZDR) | ok | ok |
| `l2-kpah-20080415-235014` | nexrad | Message 31 at legacy resolution (REF 1 km from 500 m) | ok | ok |
| `l2-klix-20050829-130035` | nexrad | Message 1 with metadata (AR2V0001, VCP 121) | ok (gunzipped input) | ok |
| `l2-ktlx-19990504-002218` | nexrad | Message 1, NUL ICAO, no location (ARCHIVE2) | error: `ValueError` conflicting azimuth sizes | ok |
| `odim-dkrom-20260820-1130-pvol` | odim | PVOL, 8 quantities, equal start/end times | ok (warns) | ok |
| `odim-iesha-20260305-0115-pvol` | odim | PVOL, gate tiers 497/350/240/100, 90 deg sweep | ok | ok |
| `odim-espdg-20260707-1927-pvol-dbzh-vradh` | odim | PVOL, float64 planes | ok | ok |
| `cfrad1-irene-sr2-20110827-120420-sur-sweeps01` | cfradial1 | PPI, int8 packed, calibration | ok | ok |
| `cfrad1-dow8-20211011-223602-rhi-trim3-classic` | cfradial1 | RHI, int16 packed, moving platform | ok | ok |
| `cfrad1-xsapr-sgp-20110520-ppi-netcdf4` | cfradial1 | PPI, float32 with `_FillValue` -9999 | ok | ok |

xradar 0.12 cannot read whole-file gzip, so gzip Level II files are decompressed for xradar only
(`reader.input = "gunzip"`, with the decompressed SHA-256). Py-ART reads the manifest file.

## Cross-reader verification (`--verify`)

Last run (2026-09-16, the versions in `index.json`), all passing:

| Case | Check | Compared | Skipped |
|---|---|---|---|
| KTLX 2024 | MetPy native moments on Py-ART's range == Py-ART hash | 140 | 0 |
| KTLX 2024 | xradar raw, ICD float32, padded == Py-ART hash | 104 | 0 |
| KDVN 2020 | MetPy -> Py-ART / xradar -> Py-ART | 126 / 101 | 0 / 0 |
| KPAH 2008 | MetPy -> Py-ART / xradar -> Py-ART | 21 / 4 | 0 / 11 (xradar geometry differs) |
| KLIX 2005 | MetPy -> Py-ART / xradar -> Py-ART | 60 / 0 | 0 / 36 (xradar geometry differs) |
| KTLX 1999 | MetPy -> Py-ART | 48 | xradar failed |
| dkrom, iesha, espdg | xradar raw masked and scaled vs Py-ART count, min, max, mean | 80, 30, 4 | 0 |
| IRENE, DOW8, xsapr | same | 4, 3, 1 | 0 |

The MetPy check places each native gate `gate_width / 250 m` times on Py-ART's 250 m range and
evaluates `(raw - offset) / scale` in float32 with raw 0 and 1 masked. It matches Py-ART
(`linear_interp=False`) bit for bit, including the 1 km reflectivity of Message 1 and
legacy-resolution volumes. Those are the values the FM301 view produces for coarse fields
(design note 6.5, `GateMapping` stride 4).

## Differences the Rust comparison has to expect

These come from the design note, and the goldens show them as the readers produce them:

- NEXRAD fields: xradar writes no `_FillValue`, `_Undetect`, `valid_range` or `flag_*` (the view
  adds them, 7.1). xradar pads short moments with raw 0, which equals the view's padding
  `_FillValue = 0`, so raw hashes match for truncated fields (stride 1).
- Coarse NEXRAD reflectivity (KLIX 2005, KPAH 2008 sweeps with 1 km REF): xradar puts the sweep
  on REF's spacing, pads REF with zeros and misplaces VRADH/WRADH by x4. It also reads the
  -375 m first gate as 65161 and emits no WRADH for Message 1. The view's layout is Py-ART's
  (`linear_interp=False`) instead (6.2, 6.5).
- NEXRAD root: xradar has no `sweep_group_name`/`sweep_fixed_angle` (the view always emits them),
  and gives Message 1 volumes integer 0 latitude/longitude/altitude (the model keeps `None`, 11).
- ODIM `TH`: xradar labels it linear and unitless; io-odim uses dBZ (8.2 note 1).
- Ray order: `time` view rays are in acquisition order (identity for NEXRAD and CfRadial;
  rotated for iesha); `auto` sorts by angle (DOW8's RHI uses dimension `azimuth`).
